summary: GRN 867 is a withdrawn GRAS notice submitted by Cargill on June 5, 2019, for rebaudioside M (Reb M) produced by a genetically engineered Yarrowia lipolytica strain, voluntarily withdrawn on August 19, 2019, before FDA completed its review. The notifier cited unspecified 'technical language' requiring clarification, stating the GRAS conclusion was unaffected. The notice presents a well-structured safety case built primarily on read-across from the extensive steviol glycoside safety database, with the pivotal metabolic bridge supported by a fecal homogenate study conducted on a compositionally similar S. cerevisiae-derived Reb M (GRN 000626) rather than the Y. lipolytica product itself. Safety data from GRN 000768 are incorporated by reference. Specifications, batch analyses for three non-consecutive lots, residual protein and DNA data, and a GRAS panel consensus statement are present. Key evidentiary gaps include: the metabolic bridge study used a different production organism's material; stability studies on the Y. lipolytica product were not yet completed at submission; and the notice does not disclose what 'technical language' prompted withdrawal, leaving an unresolved documentation question. Overall evidence readiness is moderate-to-strong for a read-across framework but contains addressable gaps in test-article specificity and stability documentation.

findings.title: Pivotal metabolic bridge study used S. cerevisiae-derived Reb M, not the Y. lipolytica target material
findings.summary: The notice acknowledges that microbial metabolism studies have not been conducted with the Y. lipolytica Reb M that is the subject of this application. The fecal homogenate hydrolysis study presented in Section 6.2.1 used steviol glycosides produced by S. cerevisiae (GRN 000626). The bridge relies on compositional similarity (both primarily rebaudioside M and D) and the shared steviol backbone metabolic pathway. While the rationale is scientifically coherent, the test article is from a different production organism, and the notice does not provide organism-specific metabolic data for the Y. lipolytica product.
findings.recommendedAction: Conduct or cite a microbial metabolism study using the Y. lipolytica-derived Reb M as the test article, or provide a more detailed compositional and process equivalence analysis demonstrating that any organism-specific differences are toxicologically irrelevant.

The notice does not reproduce the underlying studies, does not identify which specific studies are pivotal versus supportive, and does not articulate an independent analysis of that incorporated body of evidence. The notice states only that new data (July 2017–March 2019) are summarized in Section 6.4. This structure means the evidentiary foundation for the pre-July 2017 safety database is not self-contained.

findings.title: Stability studies on the Y. lipolytica Reb M product not completed at time of submission
findings.summary: Section 2.4.2 explicitly states that stability studies have not yet been conducted with the Y. lipolytica Reb M preparation. The conventional and accelerated stability studies presented (Tables 2.4.2-1 and 2.4.2-2) were conducted on S. cerevisiae-derived material (GRN 000626) and were themselves described as 'currently on-going' with only 3-month preliminary data. The stability bridge to the Y. lipolytica product relies on compositional similarity and JECFA's general conclusions for steviol glycosides.
findings.recommendedAction: Complete stability studies on the Y. lipolytica-derived Reb M product under both conventional and accelerated conditions, or provide a more detailed scientific justification for why the S. cerevisiae stability data are fully predictive of Y. lipolytica product stability, including any process-related compositional differences that could affect stability.

findings.title: EFSA 2018 disagreement on metabolic fate read-across for all steviol glycosides not fully resolved in the notice
findings.summary: Section 6.3 discloses that EFSA (2018a) did not agree to expand the definition of steviol glycosides to include all individual steviol glycosides 'because of uncertainties on the rate and extent of the metabolism of the different steviol glycosides to steviol.' The notice acknowledges this authoritative disagreement but does not provide a detailed rebuttal or additional data specifically addressing EFSA's stated uncertainty. The notice's safety case relies centrally on the shared metabolic fate argument that EFSA found insufficiently supported for a broad expansion.
findings.recommendedAction: Provide a targeted response to EFSA 2018a's specific concerns about metabolic fate uncertainty, including quantitative hydrolysis rate comparisons for rebaudioside M and D relative to rebaudioside A, and explain why the data presented in Section 6.2.1 are sufficient to address EFSA's stated uncertainties.

findings.title: BLAST toxin homology analysis reports matches up to 68% identity without structural analysis to rule out functional homology
findings.summary: Section 6.5.1 reports that BLAST searches identified sequence matches with 17 to 68% identity with animal venom proteins and toxins. The notice states that E-values greater than 1×10⁻⁷ suggest proteins are unlikely to share structural homology, and that the low E-value matches (10⁻⁹ to 10⁻⁶⁰) shared 21–31% identity with cytochrome P450 monooxygenases, which are native human enzymes. However, the notice does not provide a structural or functional analysis for the matches with higher identity (up to 68%) that had E-values above the 1×10⁻⁷ threshold, relying solely on the E-value cutoff to dismiss these matches.
findings.recommendedAction: For any BLAST matches with identity above 35% or with E-values below 1×10⁻⁷, provide a brief structural or functional analysis explaining why these matches do not indicate toxic or allergenic potential, consistent with FAO/WHO 2001 guidance.

safetySignals.label: EFSA 2018 authoritative disagreement on metabolic fate read-across
safetySignals.summary: EFSA (2018a) explicitly declined to expand the steviol glycoside definition to all individual glycosides due to uncertainties about the rate and extent of metabolism to steviol. This represents a documented authoritative disagreement with the notice's central safety argument. The notice discloses this disagreement but does not provide a targeted rebuttal with quantitative data addressing EFSA's specific concerns.
evidence: EFSA 2018a declined expansion due to metabolic fate uncertainties
Notice's safety case relies on shared metabolic fate argument
No targeted rebuttal data provided for EFSA's specific concerns

citations.excerpt: EFSA did not agree to expand the definition of steviol glycosides to include all individual steviol glycosides because of uncertainties on the rate and extent of the metabolism of the different steviol glycosides to steviol (EFSA, 2018a).
citations.section: 6.3 Summary of Safety Opinions by Scientific and Regulatory Authorities

safetySignals.label: Rebaudioside A-associated disruption of steroidogenesis in weanling rats at suprathreshold doses
safetySignals.summary: Jiang et al. (2018) reported disruption of steroidogenesis and decreased serum progesterone in weanling female rats at doses of approximately 76 and 486 mg/kg bw/day steviol equivalents (19–120 times the ADI upper limit). The notice contextualizes these findings as above-ADI and of limited human relevance. The signal is noted because the test article was rebaudioside A, a component present in Reb M, and the study used a vulnerable developmental population (weanling rats).
evidence: Jiang 2018 reported steroidogenesis disruption at 76–486 mg/kg bw/day steviol equivalents
Doses 19–120 times above ADI upper limit
Weanling rat model represents developmental vulnerability

citations.excerpt: Given that the doses of rebaudioside A utilized in this study on a steviol equivalent basis are well above the upper limit of the steviol glycoside ADI (about 19 to 120 times higher), the relevance of these data to human exposure to steviol glycosides in food is limited.
citations.section: 6.4.4 Reproductive and Developmental Toxicity

safetySignals.label: Statistically significant changes in urinary cortisol and cortisone in human clinical study
safetySignals.summary: Al-Dujaili et al. (2017) reported statistically significant increases and decreases in urinary concentrations of free cortisol and cortisone following 7 days of stevia consumption in healthy subjects. The notice notes study limitations (small sample size n=8/group, short washout, unvalidated dosage, uncharacterized purity of test article). The signal is noted because it involves a human study with a documented adverse observation, even though the authors concluded further research is needed.
evidence: Al-Dujaili 2017 reported significant urinary cortisol/cortisone changes
Small sample size (n=8/group) and uncharacterized test article purity
Authors concluded further research needed

citations.excerpt: Significant increases and decreases were observed in urinary concentrations of free cortisol and cortisone, compared to baseline. The authors noted several limitations with the study design, including small sample size, potential for recognition by subjects of difference between placebo and stevia test article, lack of validation of dosage consumed, and a short washout period and as a result, concluded that further research is needed to understand the significance of the observed effects.
citations.section: 6.4.5 Human Studies

safetySignals.label: Reported allergic and hypersensitivity reactions to stevia sweeteners attributed to impurities
safetySignals.summary: Section 3.1 discloses two cases of anaphylaxis/allergic reactions (Japan) and one hypersensitivity case (U.S.) following consumption of stevia sweeteners. The notice attributes these to impurities in products not meeting the JECFA ≥95% purity specification. While the notice's product meets this specification, the signal is noted because the causal attribution to impurities is hypothetical ('suspected by the study authors') and not definitively established.
evidence: Two anaphylaxis cases in Japan (Kimata 2007) and one hypersensitivity case in U.S. (Esmail and Kabadi 2012)
Impurity hypothesis is attributed to study authors, not confirmed
Reb M meets ≥95% purity specification

citations.excerpt: Two cases from Japan and 1 case from the U.S. have been reported wherein allergic and hypersensitivity reactions, respectively, to stevia sweeteners occurred (Kimata, 2007; Esmail and Kabadi, 2012). In these cases, the purity of the stevia sweeteners was suspected by the study authors to not meet the JECFA specification of ≥95% total steviol glycosides.

safetySignals.label: No completed stability data for Y. lipolytica Reb M at time of submission
safetySignals.summary: The notice explicitly states that stability studies have not been conducted on the Y. lipolytica Reb M product. The only stability data presented are for the S. cerevisiae-derived material (GRN 000626) and are themselves preliminary (3-month data from ongoing studies). This represents a gap in the stability evidence base for the specific product being notified.
evidence: No stability studies on Y. lipolytica Reb M
S. cerevisiae stability studies ongoing with 3-month preliminary data only
Stability bridge relies on compositional similarity and JECFA general conclusions

citations.excerpt: Stability studies have not yet been conducted with the Reb M preparation that is the subject of this Notification (i.e., steviol glycosides produced by Y. lipolytica).
